lines.text: Nobody moved. Not the Skeld. Not the hunters. Not even the wind.
Wren. You've grown.
Wren had an arrow on the string before I saw her move. Aimed at his heart.
Five years. You were alive for five years.
Yes.
Mother kept your bowl on the table. Every night. For two years.
He came to us half dead, five winters ago. We called him One-Eye. We never asked his southern name. That is not our way.
Something in the deep ice took my eye. The Skeld carried me out. By their law, a life saved is owed a year. When my year was done, the White had moved behind me.
That's one year. What about the other four?
He didn't answer. A small boy had come running out of the tents, and wrapped himself around Garrow's leg.
Papa! Papa, you're back!
The boy had red-brown hair. Like Garrow's. Like Wren's.
This is Rune. His mother was Freydis's daughter. The cold took her last winter.
Wren lowered the bow. I think it would have been easier for her if he'd been a monster.
She walked out onto the ice, a long way, and sat down in the snow.
I followed, sat beside her, and said nothing. Bram taught me that. Sometimes a lord's whole job is to sit nearby and be warm.
I used to dream he'd come home. Now he's here, and I don't know what I want.
When we came back, Ash was waiting for us. He looked extremely pleased with himself. And a white wolf watched from the trees.
Where have you been all night? ...Oh. Oh, I see.
My lord. You came for allies, and the Skeld need warmth. I know where there's more rimeglass than your smith could work in a hundred years.
The Glass Deep, under the mountain. I've been inside it once.
That's where I lost this.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter thirty-five, coming soon.
